title: The line-based echo service
description: Implement a TCP client and iterative server on 127.0.0.1:5055. Each connection sends one UTF-8 line terminated by newline; the server responds with the uppercase line plus newline, then closes the connection. The server must accept the next client. Handle data split across recv() calls. Download the lab to run sockets locally. Browser Python cannot create raw TCP connections.
starter:
import socket

# Implement the client and server in separate downloaded files.
solution:
# server.py
import socket
with socket.socket() as server:
    server.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
    server.bind(('127.0.0.1', 5055))
    server.listen()
    while True:
        connection, address = server.accept()
        with connection:
            data = b''
            while b'\n' not in data:
                chunk = connection.recv(1024)
                if not chunk:
                    break
                data += chunk
            if b'\n' in data:
                line = data.split(b'\n', 1)[0].decode('utf-8')
                connection.sendall((line.upper() + '\n').encode('utf-8'))
hints: TCP is a byte stream: a recv call is not a complete message.

def insertion_index(values, target):
    lo, hi = 0, len(values)
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi)//2
        if values[mid] < target: lo = mid + 1
        else: hi = mid
    return lo

def reverse_links(nodes, head):
    previous = -1
    while head != -1:
        nxt = nodes[head][1]
        nodes[head][1] = previous
        previous, head = head, nxt
    return previous

title: Compress repeated characters
description: Implement encode(text). Input contains lowercase ASCII letters only. Replace runs of at least three identical letters with % followed by the letter and decimal run length. Leave shorter runs unchanged.
solution:
def encode(text):
    out, i = '', 0
    while i < len(text):
        j = i+1
        while j < len(text) and text[j] == text[i]: j += 1
        count = j-i
        out += '%'+text[i]+str(count) if count >= 3 else text[i:j]
        i = j
    return out

title: Audit a magic square
description: Implement is_magic(grid). Return True only for a nonempty n×n grid containing each integer 1 through n² exactly once, with equal row, column and both diagonal sums. Reject ragged grids.
solution:
def is_magic(grid):
    n = len(grid)
    if not n or any(len(row) != n for row in grid): return False
    if sorted(v for row in grid for v in row) != list(range(1,n*n+1)): return False
    target = n*(n*n+1)//2
    return all(sum(row)==target for row in grid) and all(sum(grid[i][j] for i in range(n))==target for j in range(n)) and sum(grid[i][i] for i in range(n))==target and sum(grid[i][n-1-i] for i in range(n))==target
hints: Checking sums alone does not prove that all required values occur.

title: Construct an odd-order magic square
description: Implement make_magic(n) for positive odd n. Start with 1 in the top middle cell. Move up one and right one with wraparound. If occupied, move down one from the previous position instead. Continue to n². Return the grid.
solution:
def make_magic(n):
    a = [[0]*n for _ in range(n)]
    r, c = 0, n//2
    for value in range(1,n*n+1):
        a[r][c] = value
        nr, nc = (r-1)%n, (c+1)%n
        if a[nr][nc]: r = (r+1)%n
        else: r,c = nr,nc
    return a
hints: Calculate the candidate next cell before changing the current position.

title: Choose an eligible add-on
description: Implement eligible(items, selected_price, threshold). items are [name, integer_price] pairs. Return all items whose price plus selected_price meets the threshold, ordered by price then name. Use your own merge sort and a binary-search lower boundary. Do not mutate items or use built-in sorting.
solution:
def eligible(items, selected_price, threshold):
    def merge_sort(a):
        if len(a)<2: return a[:]
        m=len(a)//2; l=merge_sort(a[:m]); r=merge_sort(a[m:]); out=[];i=j=0
        while i<len(l) and j<len(r):
            if (l[i][1],l[i][0]) <= (r[j][1],r[j][0]): out.append(l[i]);i+=1
            else: out.append(r[j]);j+=1
        return out+l[i:]+r[j:]
    a=merge_sort(items);lo=0;hi=len(a)
    while lo<hi:
        mid=(lo+hi)//2
        if a[mid][1]+selected_price < threshold:lo=mid+1
        else:hi=mid
    return a[lo:]
hints: Sort records by (price, name), then locate the first sufficient price.

title: Import, sort, search an inventory

solution:
import csv
def inventory(path, target):
    with open(path,newline='') as f: records=[[name,int(value)] for name,value in csv.reader(f)]
    def quick(a):
        if len(a)<2:return a[:]
        p=a[0]
        return quick([x for x in a[1:] if x[0]<p[0]])+[p]+quick([x for x in a[1:] if x[0]>=p[0]])
    records=quick(records);lo=0;hi=len(records)-1
    while lo<=hi:
        mid=(lo+hi)//2
        if records[mid][0]==target:return [records,records[mid][1]]
        if records[mid][0]<target:lo=mid+1
        else:hi=mid-1
    return [records,-1]
hints: Keep file parsing, sorting and searching as separate steps.

title: Validate a sliding-tile move
description: Implement move(board, direction). board is a flat list of nine integers with 0 as the blank. direction moves the blank up/down/left/right. Return a new board after a legal move; otherwise return an unchanged copy. The input must stay unchanged.
solution:
def move(board, direction):
    out=board[:];p=out.index(0);r,c=divmod(p,3)
    dr,dc={'up':(-1,0),'down':(1,0),'left':(0,-1),'right':(0,1)}[direction]
    nr,nc=r+dr,c+dc
    if 0<=nr<3 and 0<=nc<3:
        q=nr*3+nc;out[p],out[q]=out[q],out[p]
    return out
hints: Convert the blank index into row and column before testing a move.

title: Transfer credits atomically
description: Implement transfer(conn, source, target, amount). Wallet(id, balance) stores integer balances. For a positive integer amount, transfer only if both distinct IDs exist and the source has enough funds. Return True on success, False otherwise. Invalid requests leave all balances unchanged. Use SQL parameters and a transaction.

def transfer(conn, source, target, amount):
    pass
solution:
def transfer(conn, source, target, amount):
    if source==target or type(amount) is not int or amount<=0:return False
    with conn:
        a=conn.execute('SELECT balance FROM Wallet WHERE id=?',(source,)).fetchone()
        b=conn.execute('SELECT balance FROM Wallet WHERE id=?',(target,)).fetchone()
        if a is None or b is None or a[0]<amount:return False
        conn.execute('UPDATE Wallet SET balance=balance-? WHERE id=?',(amount,source))
        conn.execute('UPDATE Wallet SET balance=balance+? WHERE id=?',(amount,target))
    return True
hints: Validate all preconditions before either UPDATE.
setup:
import sqlite3
def transfer_check(a,b,n):
    conn=sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
    conn.executescript('CREATE TABLE Wallet(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,balance INTEGER); INSERT INTO Wallet VALUES(1,100),(2,20);')
    result=transfer(conn,a,b,n)
    return [result,conn.execute('SELECT balance FROM Wallet ORDER BY id').fetchall()]

title: Allocate and recycle list nodes
description: Implement manage_list(capacity, operations) using an array-backed singly linked list and a free list. Operations are ["insert", integer] and ["delete", integer]. Keep values ascending and unique. Insert returns False for duplicates/full capacity; delete returns False if absent. Return [operation_results, final_values]. Deleted slots must be reusable. capacity is positive. Do not use list.insert/remove or a dynamic data list for storage.
solution:
def manage_list(capacity, operations):
    data=[None]*capacity; links=list(range(1,capacity))+[-1];head=-1;free=0;results=[]
    for op,value in operations:
        prev=-1;cur=head
        while cur!=-1 and data[cur]<value:prev,cur=cur,links[cur]
        found=cur!=-1 and data[cur]==value
        if op=='insert':
            if found or free==-1:results.append(False);continue
            slot=free;free=links[slot];data[slot]=value;links[slot]=cur
            if prev==-1:head=slot
            else:links[prev]=slot
            results.append(True)
        else:
            if not found:results.append(False);continue
            if prev==-1:head=links[cur]
            else:links[prev]=links[cur]
            data[cur]=None;links[cur]=free;free=cur;results.append(True)
    values=[];cur=head
    while cur!=-1:values.append(data[cur]);cur=links[cur]
    return [results,values]

title: Sort birthday records stably
description: Implement sort_birthdays(records). Each [name, YYYYMMDD] pair contains a valid date string. Use a stable merge sort by date ascending: preserve input order for equal dates. Return a new list. No built-in sort.
solution:
def sort_birthdays(records):
    if len(records)<2:return records[:]
    m=len(records)//2;l=sort_birthdays(records[:m]);r=sort_birthdays(records[m:]);out=[];i=j=0
    while i<len(l) and j<len(r):
        if l[i][1]<=r[j][1]:out.append(l[i]);i+=1
        else:out.append(r[j]);j+=1
    return out+l[i:]+r[j:]
hints: Choose from the left half when the keys are equal.

title: Find a path through a BST
description: Implement find_path(tree, target). A node is [value,left,right] or None, and the tree is a valid BST with distinct integer values. Return the list of values from the root to the target; return [] if absent.
solution:
def find_path(tree, target):
    path=[]
    while tree is not None:
        value,left,right=tree;path.append(value)
        if value==target:return path
        tree=left if target<value else right
    return []
hints: Only one child can contain the target in a BST.
